title: Quantum noise scaling in continuously operating multiparameter sensors
summary: Maps the three quantum noise sources in OPMs (photon shot noise, spin projection noise, measurement back-action) across pump/probe power parameter space. Key finding: fundamental trade-off between high-frequency sensitivity (photon shot noise limited) and low-frequency sensitivity (back-action limited). This defines the hard floor for OPM-based neural sensing.

key_numbers.noise_sources: photon shot noise, spin projection noise, measurement back-action
key_numbers.frequency_trade_off: high-freq limited by photon shot noise; low-freq limited by back-action

bci_relevance: Shot noise is the limiting floor for OPMs at neural signal frequencies (1-100 Hz). Brain MEG signals are well below shot noise limit without shielding. Entanglement-enhanced OPMs (squeezed light) can push below shot noise but add complexity and cost (~$50k+ laser systems). For independent researcher: shielding is cheaper than squeezed light.
independent_researcher_budget: Squeezed light injection adds ~$30-50k for OPO system. Mu-metal shielding box ~$2-5k. Shielding is the practical path.
